verdict.rationale: RunAnywhere's rcli accepts spoken natural-language commands such as 'navigate to google.com in safari', and the docs describe a voice session that listens, thinks, and answers out loud. A hands-on report shows such a command did nothing while the voice claimed success, and the vendor called this a known limitation of small-model tool calling. missing for 10: reliable execution of natural-language commands, first-party docs of a natural-language command interface for operating the product itself, independent confirmation that commands work.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can operate the product with natural-language commands

citations.quote: `RunAnywhere.voice` assembles speech-to-text, a language model, and text-to-speech into one session that listens, thinks, and answers out loud.
Just tried it, really cool, fun tech demo with rcli.
